What does the AI Strategy Sprint deliver and what does it cost?

AI Strategy Sprint from Dave Willemstein takes organizations from AI ambition to a board-ready strategy and roadmap. The result is a prioritized use-case roadmap, business case outlines and a governance and operating-model plan, built around four fixed decision points. The sprint takes 4-6 weeks and is priced as a fixed project fee, set out in the proposal, excluding VAT and travel expenses.
How long does the AI Strategy Sprint take?
4-6 weeks for AI Strategy Sprint. The program runs across five working sessions built around four fixed decision points: diagnose, prioritize, decide, and ship and govern.
Does the investment in the AI Strategy Sprint come out lower if an AI Readiness Assessment is already in place?
Yes: if AI Readiness Assessment is already in place, the fixed project fee for AI Strategy Sprint is lower, because the analysis has already been done.
Source: Dave Willemstein's rates and typical timelines. Updated: October 2026.
Why sprints work and lengthy programs stall
Six-month strategy programs produce a document that is already outdated by the time it lands.
AI changes faster than your decision-making cycle. A sprint forces choices while they still matter.
The decision-makers sit in the sprint itself, not only in the closing presentation. That saves three rounds of alignment.
Everything we deliver is built to support decisions, not to impress.
Four fixed decision points, spread across five working sessions.
What are we actually trying to solve? We break the ambition down into business outcomes you can measure. This usually already reveals that two of the five ambitions contradict each other.
Which use cases deserve money, time and attention? Scoring on value, feasibility, data readiness and change load. The list gets shorter, not longer.
Build, buy or partner, and why? A substantiated choice per theme, including a TCO order of magnitude and the consequences for your architecture.
How do we make sure it lands? Operating model, roles, metrics and the governance the AI Act requires, in usable form.

Answers to what you are thinking now.
What is the difference between the sprint and a longer program?+

A sprint produces decisions, a program produces documentation. We make the scope explicit upfront and work toward four concrete decision points. Anything outside that scope gets named as a follow-up question rather than pulled in.
Which people from our organization need to be involved?+

A sponsor with mandate, someone from the business who knows the P&L, someone from data or IT, and someone from risk or compliance. Four to six people in the core group. Bigger makes it slower, not better.
What if we do not have AI use cases yet?+
That is the normal starting point. We start from business outcomes and work back to use cases. Ideas already floating around get folded in, but they are never the starting point.

I do not receive commissions, affiliate fees or margin on implementation partners. If I have advised a vendor before or have a relationship with one, I disclose that before we discuss that vendor. That is also stated in the agreement.
Will you present the result to our board?+
If you want me there, I will be, for questions. But you present. A strategy your advisor has to explain is not yet yours.
